title: performance(canary): automated detection and rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Aisha Khatri
description:
Motivation: We need continuous automatic detection of latency and throughput regressions in the perf canary pipeline and stronger rollout guards to prevent bad model/service rollouts. This PR implements an autodetect detector, tight hysteresis-based rollout guards, and an operator-configurable sensitivity profile so teams can tune detection thresholds per workload.

What this PR does (summary): 1) New canary detector service (perf/canary/detector) that consumes existing perf metrics streams and runs lightweight online detection (EWMA + percentile drift + throughput anomaly scoring). 2) Adds an SDK hook to the rollout controller so the detector can gate automated traffic shifts (canary -> stable) with hysteresis and minimum-sample requirements. 3) Introduces sensitivity profiles (low/medium/high) configurable in the canary CRD and UI, with recommended defaults for latency-sensitive and throughput-sensitive workloads. 4) Integration tests and a local perf test harness that simulates injected latency/throughput regressions. 5) Observability: new metrics, dashboards, and alert rules for false-positive monitoring.

Notes: The description below contains the checklist and highlights from the review conversation. The operational config is backwards compatible: if the detector is disabled, existing rollout behavior is unchanged.

Checklist: - [x] Detector service implementation + unit tests - [x] Rollout controller gating + integration tests - [x] Sensitivity profiles + defaults - [x] Metrics and dashboards - [x] Documentation (docs/perf-canary.md) - [x] E2E perf test harness - [x] Load test run on staging without regressions

Backward compatibility and migration: By default the new detector is disabled; enabling requires adding a canary.detector.enabled=true flag in the canary CR. Customers on Dedicated/Private will see no change until they opt in.

Risk: Moderate - detection logic is conservative and includes hysteresis and minimum-sample windows to minimize false-positive rollbacks. We added a canary.fail_open flag for teams that prefer availability over automated rollback.

Follow-ups: 1) RFC for per-customer sensitivity tuning and auto-calibration (ENG-2620), 2) Add ML-based drift detector as an opt-in experimental mode (ENG-2657).

release_notes: Adds an automated canary detector service and rollout guards that can block traffic shifts on detected latency/throughput regressions. Introduces configurable sensitivity profiles and default dashboards/alerts. Detector is opt-in by default (canary.detector.enabled=false).
